stem: A Halcion prescription is five months old and has five completed refills. Which fact is dispositive?

choices.text: Use the out-of-state prescription rule when its schedule, age, and verification conditions have not been checked.
The five-refill maximum is exhausted even though the six-month period has not ended.
Process another refill because an authorization written by the prescriber overrides schedule limits.
Treat the request as an insufficient-stock partial fill and use the 72-hour remainder rule.
Handle the drug or transaction as ordinary Massachusetts Schedule VI activity.

explanation.core_reasoning: A Schedule III or IV prescription may not be filled or refilled more than six months after issue and may not be refilled more than five times unless renewed by the practitioner. triazolam (Halcion) is used for short-term treatment of insomnia. It is federal Schedule IV and Massachusetts Schedule IV; its legal consequence in this scenario follows the cited schedule-specific rule.

choice_analysis.B: This applies Federal Schedule III and IV refill limits: A Schedule III or IV prescription may not be filled or refilled more than six months after issue and may not be refilled more than five times unless renewed by the practitioner.
choice_analysis.C: That choice belongs, if at all, to Federal Schedule III and IV refill limits; its trigger does not match this scenario.
choice_analysis.D: That choice belongs, if at all, to Schedule II partial fill caused by pharmacy inability; its trigger does not match this scenario.
choice_analysis.E: That choice belongs, if at all, to Massachusetts Schedule VI prescription-drug status; its trigger does not match this scenario.
